title: Fractal shot mixer playlog
content:
Purpose: running a lightweight exploration of mixing small exemplar sets (shots) from different domains to reduce brittle hallucinations and improve instruction grounding. This is a personal playlog — messy, partial, experiments + mental models. Not for sharing yet.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Combining a small number (2-4) of high-quality domain-proximal shots + 1 generic framing shot gives better factual precision than 4 domain shots alone, in low-token budgets.
- Rotating the order of the framing shot (front vs. middle) changes output style more than content fidelity; position matters for style steering.

Experimental design notes:
- Model: internal-hosted gpt-like v2 (sequence length 1024); use temp 0.2 for most runs.
- Metric quick-checks: hallucination flag (binary), concise_score (0-4 subjective), adherence_to_task (0-4). Manual labels for 50 prompts.
- Batch setup: 30 prompts drawn from customer-support and product-faq domain. Each prompt: user question + context snippet (~60 tokens).
- Variants: A (4 domain shots), B (3 domain + 1 framing front), C (1 framing front + 3 domain), D (2 domain + 1 generic + 1 counterexample shot).

Run 001 (notes):
- Seed prompt set: support tickets about billing (invoice mismatch, prorated credits), 30 items.
- Quick observation: B (framing front) gave fewer hallucinations than A, about -18% on manual labels. C (framing middle) gave more concise answers but slightly higher omission failures.
- Noted failure pattern: when framing used a too-formal example, model over-apologized and added policy text not in knowledge base. Need neutral-tone framing.

Examples (raw templates used):
- Framing shot (neutral):
  "User: I was billed twice for invoice #12345, the charge looks wrong.
   Agent: Sorry about the confusion — I checked the invoice and found a duplicate charge posted on 2025-09-12. We will refund the duplicate within 5 business days. If you want faster handling, reply with 'refund now' and include last 4 of the card."

- Domain shot (faq-style):
  "User: How are prorated credits applied?
   Agent: Prorated credits are applied at the next invoice cycle and appear as a line item 'prorated adjustment'. They reduce the total due; credits do not expire for 12 months."

- Counterexample shot (what not to do):
  "User: Where is the invoice?
   Agent: Check the billing tab in settings, then click 'download invoice'. (Incorrect: do not claim invoices are downloadable if customer is on old plan)"

Observed brittle cases (qualitative):
- When the domain shot references a product page by name, the model invents a URL if memory cutoff unclear. Fix: include explicit 'no external links' instruction in framing.
- Repetition loop: mixing two near-identical shots causes the model to echo both variants and produce overly verbose duplication. Solution: collapse near-duplicates during exemplar selection.
- Token budget trade-offs: adding a generic short framing shot (~30 tokens) typically improved grounding more than adding a second domain shot of similar length.

Selection heuristics I'm testing (todo):
- Diversity threshold: ensure pairwise token-wise edit distance > 0.3 among shots to avoid mirror examples.
- Tone anchor: include at least one shot that models the desired politeness level (neutral/warm/concise).
- Negative signal: include 1 explicit counterexample to teach what to avoid when model tends to hallucinate.

Few-shot bank snapshot (for reuse):
- bank/fractal-1: 3 domain (billing) + framing front (neutral) — good for billing support
- bank/fractal-2: 2 domain (billing + subscription change) + generic safety shot + counterexample — useful for multi-topic queries

Failure catalogue (short):
- Case F1: hallucinated policy citations ("per company policy, X") — likely from training leakage. Short-term mitigation: add "do not fabricate policies" explicit instruction in framing.
- Case F2: invented dates (e.g., refund timeline shorter than policy) — mitigation: anchor with 'check account page' fallback and avoid concrete timelines unless in KB.
- Case F3: verbose duplication when two close shots overlap — mitigation: dedupe or compress to single canonical exemplar.

Quick action items:
- [ ] Run 200-item batch with automated hallucination classifier (GH: repro-playbooks#412) and collect precision/recall for variants A-D.
- [ ] Add small automated script to compute pairwise embedding distance between shots and flag near-duplicates. Track histogram of distances.
- [ ] Try swapping framing shot tone (warm vs neutral vs terse) and measure concise_score delta.
- [ ] Build a quick 'negative-example' library: 30 examples where the right behavior is to refuse or to ask for account verification.

Notes to self (random):
- Keep framing short (<40 tokens) unless context distribution demands more.
- For enterprise customers: avoid any mention of refund timelines unless explicitly in contract.
- Remember: rotating the framing position is cheap — automate A/B position inside search/templating layer.

Logged anomalies during manual review:
- Example id 17: model returns an email address not present in KB. Add rule to sanitize personal/contact info unless exactly matched in account context.
- Example id 24: model paraphrases policy incorrectly after mixing counterexample. Possibly the counterexample primed the wrong verbatim phrasing. Reduce counterexample concreteness.

References and pointers:
- Confluence quick notes: CON-4821 (prompt engineering patterns) — see section 'framing as anchor'.
- GH repro run: redwood/repro-playbooks#412 — has dataset + eval script for hallucination classifier.

Closing thoughts (for now):
- Prompts are graceful only if selection heuristics are enforced (dupe removal, tone anchor). The simplest wins: 1 neutral framing front + 2 domain shots often beats 4 domain shots in our small tests.
- Next run: automate distance checks and run at scale, collect stable metrics before any rollout.

Scratch history: 2025-11-02 initial idea; 2026-01-15 first manual run; 2026-02-14 notes update after second manual sweep.

End of playlog (for now).
